title: Quantum-state texture measure and texture transformation
authors: Yufan Lin, Yu Guo, Fei He, Shuanping Du
abstract: Quantum-state texture quantifies structural irregularities of a state in a selected basis and has emerged as a valuable resource for gate characterization in universal circuits. Consequently, a class of contractive distance based texture measures and a framework for constructing convex-roof extended texture measure have been proposed. Here, we extend this theory in several directions. We examine the convertibility of a pure state to any state under texture-free operations, and fully solve the deterministic transformation problem between any two states in the qubit case. We then propose two classes of texture measures: convex-function-based measures and texture cost defined via minimal cost of texture contained in pure states. Moreover, we show that every texture monotone gives rise to a non-negative function which admits the same properties as the function used in the convex-roof extension---thus providing a converse to that construction. Our work thereby offers a relatively comprehensive resource-theoretic formulation of quantum-state texture.
summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive resource theory for quantum-state texture, quantifying structural irregularities in quantum states. It develops new texture measures and solves the deterministic transformation problem for qubits under texture-preserving operations. The work's main contribution is proving a converse theorem that systematically characterizes all possible texture monotones.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a comprehensive resource-theoretic formulation for quantum-state texture (QST) and systematically investigate state transformation problems under texture-free operations.
main_result: The authors establish that every texture monotone corresponds to a non-negative function satisfying specific mathematical properties, providing a converse to the convex-roof extension construction for QST.
method: The work involves defining and comparing multiple texture measures (e.g., trace distance, fidelity, relative entropy) and applying resource theory concepts to characterize state transformations.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum states $ho$ on a Hilbert space $H$ (including qubits), using the uniform superposition state $	au_f$ as a reference state for texture quantification.

important_parameters: The dimension of the Hilbert space ($d$), and the parameters governing specific measures (e.g., $\mu$ for Tsallis entropy).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on defining 'texture-free operations' (CPTP maps preserving the reference state) and assuming the existence of 'resource monotones' satisfying specific properties (T1)-(T5).
paper_structure: The paper reviews existing texture measures, proposes new classes (convex-function-based), solves the deterministic transformation problem for qubits, and culminates in proving the converse relationship between texture monotones and derived functions.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, resource-theoretic framework to quantify structural imperfections (texture) in quantum states, which is crucial for characterizing the limitations of quantum gates and circuits.
